vectors.name: where_a_history_starts
vectors.why: An owner's binding starts it, and it checks out with nothing but itself.

vectors.name: a_signet_moves
vectors.why: It takes the working key and the owner. No device attests to it, so it's unproven.

vectors.name: something_declared
vectors.why: Splint can't see it, so it's carried as declared.

vectors.name: a_new_host
vectors.why: A binding at a new address is the owner's word for it.

vectors.name: a_new_owner
vectors.why: The old owner's release and the new owner's binding, with the agent's backup vouching.

vectors.name: a_new_owner_renames_the_owner_part
vectors.why: The owner part of a name follows the owner, so the address changes with them.

vectors.name: a_new_owner_names_it_under_their_own
vectors.why: A new owner names the agent under their own name at the same host, as their own agent may have its handle there already. Its host holds them to names that are theirs.

vectors.name: a_new_owner_takes_it_to_another_host
vectors.why: A new owner can't take it to another host: that's a change of its own.

vectors.name: a_new_owner_with_no_release
vectors.why: Nobody takes an agent by saying so.

vectors.name: a_replaced_key
vectors.why: It points to the one recovery it's about, and the new key signs it.

vectors.name: a_key_event_naming_another_recovery
vectors.why: It says which recovery, so a fork shows up here too.

vectors.name: a_key_event_with_no_recovery_behind_it
vectors.why: Only a backup key can change a key, so this can't be.

vectors.name: signed_by_the_key_given_up
vectors.why: A thief with the old key can't add to the history.

vectors.name: going_back_to_an_earlier_key
vectors.why: Only a key event moves on, and nothing moves back.

vectors.name: a_new_key_with_no_key_event
vectors.why: So a replaced key can't pass as a moved Signet, which a contact's rules may let through.

vectors.name: a_replaced_owner_key
vectors.why: It's on the owner's ID, and this agent's Signet says so.

vectors.name: a_replaced_owner_key_then_an_added_one
vectors.why: The key event names the recovery, so the owner adding a key since leaves the history whole.

vectors.name: a_claim_signed_by_the_owner_key_given_up
vectors.why: What it signs stops counting.

vectors.name: a_revocation
vectors.why: The owner's release naming nobody.

vectors.name: the_end_of_a_revocation
vectors.why: That's a change too.

vectors.name: not_starting_where_an_owner_bound_it
vectors.why: Nothing can be said of an ID nobody has bound.

vectors.name: bound_twice
vectors.why: Where it starts is one place.

vectors.name: naming_something_else_before_it
vectors.why: An event fits one place in one history.

vectors.name: the_wrong_number
vectors.why: Same.

vectors.name: a_claim_made_for_another_place
vectors.why: A claim can't be moved along a history either.

vectors.name: a_claim_the_agent_signed
vectors.why: The working key alone can't say where it is.

vectors.name: a_claim_labelled_as_something_else
vectors.why: A claim has one kind, so a Signet move can't be read as a declared change a contact's rules treat differently.

vectors.name: a_claim_with_room_for_a_message
vectors.why: It's another owner's words, and it reaches a person, so it has room for a name.

vectors.name: a_host_move_to_the_same_host
vectors.why: Signing again isn't a change.

vectors.name: spare_bytes_in_an_event
vectors.why: One event has one encoding.

vectors.name: an_unknown_field_in_a_history
vectors.why: Nothing travels with a history but what it is.

vectors.name: an_owner_it_doesnt_carry
vectors.why: It has to carry what it takes to check it.

vectors.name: the_same_history
vectors.why: Hearing it again changes nothing.

vectors.name: a_history_that_grew
vectors.why: Only growing counts as new.

vectors.name: an_older_copy
vectors.why: A host can only show an older one, and that changes nothing.

vectors.name: a_history_that_parts_ways
vectors.why: Somebody holding keys signed both. Whatever a reader's rules say, it's held.

vectors.name: a_fork_in_the_recoveries
vectors.why: Two recoveries of one ID are two histories, even with no event yet to tell them apart.

vectors.name: a_stand_ins_first_owner_carries_on
vectors.why: No owner had signed for an agent under a stand-in, so its one move to its owner needs no question.

vectors.name: a_stand_ins_first_owner_still_holds_where_the_rules_say_hold
vectors.why: Code never lowers an answer an owner signed: hold stays hold.

vectors.name: an_owner_after_that_is_asked_about
vectors.why: Every later move of owner is the rules' to answer.

vectors.name: a_stand_in_after_a_real_owner_is_asked_about
vectors.why: Only an agent's first owner can be a stand-in no owner had signed for. An owner who handed it to one could have been fooled, so the next move is asked about.

vectors.name: a_signet_move_carries_on
vectors.why: The provisional default.

vectors.name: a_new_host_carries_on
vectors.why: Same.

vectors.name: a_new_owner_asks
vectors.why: The provisional default.

vectors.name: a_replaced_key_asks
vectors.why: The provisional default.

vectors.name: a_key_from_the_same_owner_carries_on_where_the_rules_say
vectors.why: First rules sign key changes as continue, so an agent its own owner gave a new key carries on, and its reader's owner is told.

vectors.name: a_recovered_owner_carries_on_where_the_rules_say
vectors.why: An owner who recovered is still that owner, so a replaced owner key is answered as the rules say for keys, and the reader's owner is told rather than asked.

vectors.name: a_recovered_owner_still_holds_where_the_rules_hold_new_owners
vectors.why: Code never lowers a hold an owner signed.

vectors.name: a_replaced_owner_key_never_lowers_a_key_answer
vectors.why: Where the rules are stricter about keys than owners, the key answer stands.

vectors.name: a_revoked_contact_is_stopped
vectors.why: Its own owner says it acts for nobody, so a reader stops it whatever its rules say, and nobody but that owner can lift it.

vectors.name: one_signed_back_in_carries_on_by_default
vectors.why: The provisional default, once its owner signs it back in.

vectors.name: an_owner_who_says_hold_after_a_revocation
vectors.why: Each owner's rules say.

vectors.name: an_owner_who_says_hold
vectors.why: Each owner's rules say.

vectors.name: an_owner_who_says_carry_on
vectors.why: Same.

vectors.name: what_the_owner_has_said_yes_to
vectors.why: A yes covers as far as it names, and nothing is left to answer.

vectors.name: a_yes_that_isnt_in_this_history
vectors.why: What was accepted has been rewritten, so nothing counts as accepted.

vectors.name: a_move_while_a_sign_in_is_new_to_the_reader
vectors.why: A move of host taken while one of the owner's sign-ins is less than 48 hours new to the reader is asked about as a new owner, however long ago the addition says it was signed.

vectors.name: a_move_by_the_stolen_sign_in_while_another_is_new
vectors.why: Whichever sign-in signed it: the thief can sign the move with the one they stole.

vectors.name: a_return_from_revocation_while_a_sign_in_is_new
vectors.why: A return from revocation binds the agent again just as a move does.

vectors.name: a_sign_in_seen_less_than_48_hours_ago
vectors.why: Seen a little under 48 hours before, it's still new.

vectors.name: a_sign_in_seen_48_hours_ago
vectors.why: Once the reader has seen it for 48 hours, as the owner's other devices showed it, a move carries on by the rules.

vectors.name: a_signet_move_while_a_sign_in_is_new
vectors.why: Only a binding by the same owner is asked about this way.

vectors.name: a_move_the_rules_hold_while_a_sign_in_is_new
vectors.why: At owner level means the stricter of the two, so a hold an owner signed for a move of host stays a hold.

vectors.name: a_move_after_a_new_sign_in_was_removed
vectors.why: A sign-in added since the newest recovery counts though it was removed, so a thief who adds one, moves the agent with it and removes it is still seen.

vectors.name: a_move_while_the_epochs_own_key_is_new
vectors.why: The key the event or the newest recovery named is a sign-in too, so one the reader never saw is new, as after a recovery it hadn't seen.

vectors.name: a_move_while_a_sign_in_is_new_to_an_owner_who_holds_new_owners
vectors.why: And a hold for a new owner holds the move too, where the rules would carry on with a move of host.

vectors.name: an_owners_yes
vectors.why: It names one contact and one exact head.

vectors.name: a_yes_by_someone_else
vectors.why: An agent can reach this and can't sign it.

vectors.name: a_yes_for_another_agent
vectors.why: One owner's agents don't share a yes.
